findings.problem: This story card packs in more than two things: God gives Saul son of Kish, who rules forty years (Acts 13:21); God removes Saul and raises up a new king (Acts 13:22); and God's testimony about that king (Acts 13:22). That is three beats on one card, so it should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke "When my stamps came out crooked, I slid behind the takeout menus, friend, and nobody PROCLAIMED a thing" doesn't click. Acts 13:38 is about forgiveness of sins being proclaimed, but his crooked stamps weren't a sin, and it isn't clear what anyone should have proclaimed. It also reads like a complaint about the Millers, which doesn't fit his no-grudge character.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Pilate first shows up here (Acts 13:28) with no word on who he is. The new-people rule wants a simple description, like "Cyrus, king of Persia." But Acts 13:13-52 never says who Pilate is, and prep-walkthrough.md says every fact comes from the passage text in the BSB.
findings.question: When the passage itself never says who a new person is (here Pilate), may Papa Dorin describe him from elsewhere in the Bible (for example "Pilate, the governor"), or should he leave the name with no description?

findings.problem: Several choice cards repeat context from an earlier verse in the question, but their "verses" field cites only the right answer's verse. Stop 2 card 4 ("After the time of the judges", Acts 13:20) cites Acts 13:21. Stop 2 card 10 ("the people of Jerusalem and their rulers", Acts 13:27) cites Acts 13:28. Stop 2 card 12 ("the tomb where they laid Him after taking Him down from the tree", Acts 13:29) cites Acts 13:30. Stop 2 card 14 ("after God raised Jesus from the dead", Acts 13:30) cites Acts 13:31. Stop 3 card 6 ("crowds gathered to hear Paul", Acts 13:44) cites Acts 13:45. Stop 3 card 11 (turning to the Gentiles and the light-for-the-Gentiles quote, Acts 13:46-47) cites Acts 13:48. The Scripture rules say a reference runs "from the first verse a card uses to the last". The Output section says a choice card's verses field "is the verses of the right answer too". Both can't be true when the question uses a verse the answer doesn't.
findings.question: For a choice card, does the one verses field cover every verse the question uses (so stop 2 card 12 would be Acts 13:29-30), or only the right answer's verse (Acts 13:30)? Is context the question repeats from an earlier card exempt?
